items.title: Automated testing is the discovery-first verification owner
items.statement: The owner discovers test capabilities, probes harnesses, binds tests to WorkNode request contracts, records receipts, handles visual/browser/device evidence, and blocks completion when automated verification is absent.

evidence.exact_quote: The Automated Testing System is the plans-to-code owner for platform-capability-discovery-first verification. It defines how Puppet Master discovers available test capabilities, probes project harnesses, binds tests to WorkNode request contracts, records test receipts, handles visual/browser/device evidence, and blocks completion when automated verification is missing.

items.title: The document is policy-only and non-executable
items.statement: The owner explicitly does not create execution artifacts, dispatches, implementation files, or production build tasks.

evidence.exact_quote: This document is a contract and policy owner. It does not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, product implementation files, dispatched GoalRuns, or production build tasks.

items.title: Consumers and cross-owner boundaries are named
items.statement: Compilation, execution, artifact, GUI, tools, and shared-contract owners consume or implement this policy through explicitly divided ownership boundaries.

evidence.exact_quote: - `Plans/Plan_To_Node_Compilation.md` consumes test capability and test binding requirements while drafting non-executable NodeSeed candidates, WorkGraph drafts, and WorkNode requests.
- `Plans/Tools.md` owns concrete tool behavior for browser, GUI, device, CLI, and project-native testing helpers.
- `Plans/Contracts_V0.md` owns shared envelope fields and schema references for receipts that cross runtime boundaries.

items.title: Canonical testing report families are fixed
items.statement: The canonical report families are TestCapabilityReport, TestHarnessProbeReport, TestStrategy, and TestRunReceipt.

evidence.exact_quote: The canonical report families are TestCapabilityReport, TestHarnessProbeReport, TestStrategy, and TestRunReceipt.

items.title: GUI capability policy has global and project projections
items.statement: The production GUI exposes global and per-project capability rows with inherited/effective state plus Auto, On, Off, unavailable, authority-blocked, and policy-prohibited projections; the three choice states have distinct behavioral consequences.

evidence.exact_quote: Testing capability policy is implementation-ready only when the GUI exposes concrete controls and receipts, not merely policy prose. The production GUI must provide global and per-project rows for each capability family with inherited/effective state, `Auto`, `On`, `Off`, unavailable, blocked-needs-authority, and prohibited-by-policy projections. `Auto` may discover/select/install within authority; `On` blocks or asks for authority when unavailable; `Off` prohibits use and installation and never counts as successful verification.

items.title: Visible testing commands emit policy-bound receipts
items.statement: Six required testing commands must emit receipt evidence bound to policy snapshot, session identity, artifacts, redaction, currentness, and fallback route.

evidence.exact_quote: The required command rows are `cmd.testing.capability_policy.set`, `cmd.testing.visibility_policy.set`, `cmd.testing.session.open`, `cmd.testing.session.watch`, `cmd.testing.session.background`, and `cmd.testing.session.redaction.inspect`. Each command must produce receipt evidence linked to the effective policy snapshot, visible-session identity, artifact/evidence refs, redaction profile, currentness/revalidation result, and fallback route when a visual surface cannot be embedded.

items.title: Web and native visible evidence capabilities are enumerated
items.statement: Visible testing supports active, collapsed, detached, backgrounded, and non-embeddable projections and enumerates evidence types for web and native application testing.

evidence.exact_quote: Visible testing projections must include `show_when_possible`, visible active, collapsed, detached, backgrounded, and non-embeddable states. Web evidence must show browser navigation, clicks, form input, assertions, screenshots, console, network, and pass/fail progression where supported. Native evidence must show Swift/live preview, hot reload, simulator, emulator, physical device stream, application window, interaction trace, screenshots, and logs where available and permitted.

items.title: Browser manifests carry unavailable remediation and fallback evidence
items.statement: Browser/GUI manifests carry runtime identity, visibility/Open/Watch state, unavailable remediation actions, artifact refs, and redaction refs; negative fixtures cover browser, network, host, robots, fanout, depth, cache, and partial-outcome failures.

evidence.exact_quote: Browser and GUI automation manifests must carry `browser_session_id`, PM-native browser runtime state, visibility state, Open/Watch state, `runtime_unavailable` remediation actions, PageRepresentation refs, screenshot/PDF/console/network artifact refs, and redaction manifest refs. Playwright/CDP may appear only as fallback or reference test-driver evidence; PM-managed native browser sessions are the product runtime identity. Negative fixtures cover no-browser/runtime-unavailable, hidden prompt-injection chips, redaction failure, no-network denial, SSRF/private-host denial, robots/fanout/depth denial, cache hit/miss/TTL, and partial crawl/research/source citation outcomes.

items.title: Sensitive evidence is redacted before display or persistence
items.statement: Secret and sensitive-data redaction precedes display or persistence, and a redaction failure blocks both until resolution or explicit policy authorization.

evidence.exact_quote: Screenshots, videos, logs, console output, network traces, and artifact previews apply secret and sensitive-data redaction before display or persistence. Redaction failures block display/persistence until resolved or explicitly authorized by the owning policy; they do not silently downgrade evidence quality.

items.title: Web preview requires local trust controls and production opt-in
items.statement: The Slint/WASM development workflow must prove daemon probes, pairing/origin/CSRF controls, degradation, capture evidence, and reload behavior; production requires explicit configuration and permission/audit receipts before dev/test controls are enabled.

evidence.exact_quote: The Slint/WASM web GUI development workflow uses a trusted local daemon plus a static web route, fixture mode, browser automation smoke tests, screenshots/state capture, deterministic state hooks, and fast rebuild/reload loops. The test harness must prove daemon capability probes, pairing/origin/CSRF protections, degraded reasons when the daemon is absent or narrowed, screenshot and state-capture evidence, and reload behavior for the static web route. Production builds must not enable dev/test, MCP, live-preview, fixture, or browser automation controls unless explicit configuration enables the capability and records permission/audit receipts.

items.title: Capability discovery and harness probe precede test readiness
items.statement: Discovery runs before generation or execution and records platform/tool capabilities and research need; harness probing records commands, adapters, artifacts, flake policy, and gaps before test-ready status.

evidence.exact_quote: Test Capability Discovery must run before test generation or execution. It detects project_platform, framework/toolkit, local_capabilities, installed tools, app launch ability, browser automation, GUI automation, device/emulator automation, screenshot support, logs, headless/headed support, project-native test runners, and whether current official testing options need online research. Test Harness Probe records runnable verification commands, required adapters, expected artifacts, flake policy, and gaps before Executor treats a WorkNode request as test-ready.

items.title: Test strategy binds WorkNodes to project-specific oracles
items.statement: Each WorkNode request is bound to capabilities, harnesses, tests, commands, environment/session requirements, evidence, artifacts, flake policy, and gap policy, with oracle families selected by project type.

evidence.exact_quote: Test Strategy v2 binds each WorkNode request to required_capability_refs, required harnesses, generated or reused tests, generated_test_ids, reused_test_ids, completion commands, browser/session requirements, emulator requirements, visual evidence requirements, expected artifacts, flake policy, and test_gap_policy. The strategy must choose project-type-specific oracles: browser DOM, console, network, screenshot, and visual checks for web; launch, window, screenshot, and accessibility checks for desktop GUI; emulator/device logs and screenshots for mobile; API, contract, and database checks for backend work; exit, output, and filesystem checks for CLI work; and unit, property, and API contracts for libraries.

items.title: Automated completion blocks unverifiable work
items.statement: Human eyeballing cannot be required; required checks and capture run automatically, and inability to verify after runtime enablement produces a blocker or deferred non-executable harness candidate rather than a pass.

evidence.exact_quote: WorkNode completion cannot require human eyeballing. Tests, smoke checks, app launch, browser sessions, GUI/device sessions, screenshots, logs, and evidence capture run automatically where required. If Puppet Master cannot automatically verify a WorkNode after the compiler/runtime boundary is explicitly enabled, it must record a test capability blocker or deferred non-executable test-harness WorkNode request candidate rather than silently passing. For web projects, once the native product is built, Puppet Master built-in browser automation is the primary native web test automation path; Playwright can be optional, fallback, or project-native, not the native default.

items.title: Run receipts carry provenance and policy fields
items.statement: A TestRunReceipt records strategy and case references, generated/reused test IDs, command, artifacts, evidence, visual evidence, flake policy, and gap policy.

evidence.exact_quote: Automated completion means 100% automated verification with no human intervention for required browser/GUI/device sessions; Playwright optional remains fallback/project-native, and manual_only_acceptance_not_allowed blocks manual-only completion claims. TestRunReceipt records include receipt_id, test_strategy_ref, test_case_refs, generated_test_ids, reused_test_ids, verification_command, expected_artifacts, evidence_refs, visual_evidence_refs, flake_policy, and test_gap_policy.

items.title: Governance and schema validation establish current contract acceptance
items.statement: Acceptance uses plan index and governance validation, the handoff schema, the PRD/planning packet, and Executor rejection of missing bindings; executable harness proof is deferred until runtime/compiler enablement.

evidence.exact_quote: Acceptance for this owner doc is established by PlanUnit index validation, standard plan governance gates, the plans-to-code handoff schema, the PRD/planning runtime contract packet, and Executor intake contracts that reject missing required test bindings.

Current contract validators check TestCapabilityReport, TestHarnessProbeReport, TestStrategy, TestRunReceipt, visible evidence, and test-gap blocker shapes as schema contracts; executable test harness proof is required only after the runtime/compiler boundary is explicitly enabled.

items.title: Capability policy precedence and authority resolution are unspecified
items.statement: The text names global/per-project inherited and effective states and says Auto acts 'within authority', but does not define override precedence, conflict resolution, authority identity, approval durability, or how an effective state is computed.
items.impact: Different builders can compute different effective policies or install capabilities under different authority assumptions.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent the policy merge algorithm and authority-check contract.

evidence.exact_quote: Testing capability policy is implementation-ready only when the GUI exposes concrete controls and receipts, not merely policy prose. The production GUI must provide global and per-project rows for each capability family with inherited/effective state, `Auto`, `On`, `Off`, unavailable, blocked-needs-authority, and prohibited-by-policy projections. `Auto` may discover/select/install within authority; `On` blocks or asks for authority when unavailable; `Off` prohibits use and installation and never counts as successful verification.

items.title: Visible-session transition and recovery semantics are incomplete
items.statement: The state names and Open/Watch/background commands are present, but valid transitions, terminal states, concurrency rules, reconnect behavior, and the exact recovery path from runtime_unavailable or non-embeddable are not specified.
items.impact: Session behavior and receipts can diverge across implementations, especially after detach, backgrounding, or runtime loss.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must define a session state machine and recovery/idempotency rules.

evidence.exact_quote: Visible testing projections must include `show_when_possible`, visible active, collapsed, detached, backgrounded, and non-embeddable states. Web evidence must show browser navigation, clicks, form input, assertions, screenshots, console, network, and pass/fail progression where supported. Native evidence must show Swift/live preview, hot reload, simulator, emulator, physical device stream, application window, interaction trace, screenshots, and logs where available and permitted.

Acceptance coverage must prove effective-policy receipts, visible-session receipts, TestRunReceipt linkage, Open/Watch fallback behavior, background continuation, disabled reason projection, and redaction-before-display/persistence. PMConcept browser/terminal/testing demos are `concept_fixture_only` until those receipts and wiring rows exist.

items.title: Testing command contracts lack request and failure semantics
items.statement: The required command names and receipt links are specified, but request parameters, result discriminants, error codes, authorization failures, idempotency, cancellation, and retry behavior are absent from this authoritative window.
items.impact: Command producers and consumers cannot independently implement interoperable invocation and failure handling.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent command envelopes and lifecycle semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: The required command rows are `cmd.testing.capability_policy.set`, `cmd.testing.visibility_policy.set`, `cmd.testing.session.open`, `cmd.testing.session.watch`, `cmd.testing.session.background`, and `cmd.testing.session.redaction.inspect`. Each command must produce receipt evidence linked to the effective policy snapshot, visible-session identity, artifact/evidence refs, redaction profile, currentness/revalidation result, and fallback route when a visual surface cannot be embedded.

items.title: Flake policy semantics are named but not defined
items.statement: Flake policy is a required probe, strategy, and receipt field, yet the window does not define classification criteria, retry budgets, quarantine behavior, pass/fail aggregation, or how a flaky result affects completion.
items.impact: The same test outcomes can yield inconsistent completion decisions and receipts.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose retry and completion semantics for flaky tests.

evidence.exact_quote: TestCapabilityReport and TestHarnessProbeReport fields include online_research, automation_surface, requires_browser, requires_emulator, requires_display, requires_screenshot, verification_command, expected_artifacts, and flake_policy.

items.title: Redaction authorization exception lacks a bounded contract
items.statement: The policy allows explicit authorization after redaction failure but does not define the authorizer, scope, duration, required receipt, user warning, immutable audit evidence, or whether display and persistence may be separately authorized.
items.impact: A builder-chosen exception path could disclose or persist secrets without a consistent, auditable consent boundary.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must invent the sensitive-data exception contract.

evidence.exact_quote: Screenshots, videos, logs, console output, network traces, and artifact previews apply secret and sensitive-data redaction before display or persistence. Redaction failures block display/persistence until resolved or explicitly authorized by the owning policy; they do not silently downgrade evidence quality.

items.title: Scale and performance policies have no concrete limits
items.statement: The window requires fanout/depth denials and cache TTL behavior, but provides no budgets, defaults, concurrency limits, evidence size/retention limits, timeout policy, or performance acceptance thresholds.
items.impact: Automation can become resource-unbounded or produce incompatible denial and cache behavior.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose operational limits and performance oracles.

evidence.exact_quote: Browser and GUI automation manifests must carry `browser_session_id`, PM-native browser runtime state, visibility state, Open/Watch state, `runtime_unavailable` remediation actions, PageRepresentation refs, screenshot/PDF/console/network artifact refs, and redaction manifest refs. Playwright/CDP may appear only as fallback or reference test-driver evidence; PM-managed native browser sessions are the product runtime identity. Negative fixtures cover no-browser/runtime-unavailable, hidden prompt-injection chips, redaction failure, no-network denial, SSRF/private-host denial, robots/fanout/depth denial, cache hit/miss/TTL, and partial crawl/research/source citation outcomes.

items.title: Schema and receipt migration behavior is unspecified
items.statement: The artifact families are located in one design-only schema draft, but the window supplies no version negotiation, compatibility rules, migration path, or behavior for older TestStrategy and TestRunReceipt shapes.
items.impact: Future schema evolution can strand stored receipts or cause incompatible producer/consumer behavior.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must decide whether to reject, upgrade, or interpret older artifacts.

evidence.exact_quote: Automated testing contracts are represented in `Plans/plans_to_code_handoff.schema.json` as design-only `$defs` and artifact families, including `test_capability_report`, `test_harness_probe_report`, `test_strategy`, `test_case`, `test_run_receipt`, and `visual_evidence`. These names are schema definitions inside the single plans-to-code handoff schema draft; they are not separate runtime queues or emitted product artifacts.

items.title: Oracle selection does not define deterministic pass criteria
items.statement: Project-specific oracle families are named, but the window does not define required combinations, assertion thresholds, screenshot comparison tolerances, accessibility pass criteria, or the rule that selects among multiple available oracles.
items.impact: Two compliant strategies can test different evidence and disagree on whether identical work passes.
items.builder_discretion: Builders must choose oracle combinations and thresholds.

evidence.exact_quote: Test Strategy v2 binds each WorkNode request to required_capability_refs, required harnesses, generated or reused tests, generated_test_ids, reused_test_ids, completion commands, browser/session requirements, emulator requirements, visual evidence requirements, expected artifacts, flake policy, and test_gap_policy. The strategy must choose project-type-specific oracles: browser DOM, console, network, screenshot, and visual checks for web; launch, window, screenshot, and accessibility checks for desktop GUI; emulator/device logs and screenshots for mobile; API, contract, and database checks for backend work; exit, output, and filesystem checks for CLI work; and unit, property, and API contracts for libraries.

dimension_assessments.summary: Discovery-first verification, binding, automated execution, blocker routing, and scope boundaries are explicit.
Discovery, browser, GUI, device, web preview, evidence, and harness capabilities are enumerated.
Report families, discovery/probe fields, strategy bindings, evidence refs, and TestRunReceipt fields are specified.
Artifact and binding contracts are extensive, but testing command request/failure semantics are absent.
Visible states are listed without a complete transition, concurrency, or recovery state machine.
Production, installation, and redaction authority boundaries exist but effective-policy and exception authorization are under-specified.
The automated-testing owner and adjacent concrete-tool, GUI, artifact, and contract owners are named.
Compilation, Executor, artifact, runtime-panel, GUI, tools, and shared-contract consumers are named.
Capability policy controls, visible-session projections, web/native evidence, and production preview restrictions are explicit.
Blockers, unavailable remediation, fallback, and redaction blocking exist, but session and command recovery semantics remain incomplete.
Pairing/origin/CSRF, SSRF/private-host denial, prompt-injection fixtures, and redaction-before-display are covered, but the redaction exception is not safely bounded.
Test policy propagates through compilation, Executor, receipt/evidence artifacts, GUI projections, and shared runtime envelopes.
Current governance/schema validation and runtime-disabled/deferred implementation boundaries are explicit.
Fanout, depth, cache, and partial outcomes are named without concrete resource or latency limits.
Playwright fallback compatibility is explicit, but schema/receipt version evolution and migration are not.
Project-type oracle families and current validators are named, but deterministic oracle combinations and thresholds are not.
Builders retain consequential discretion over policy merge, command envelopes, state transitions, retries, resource budgets, migration, and oracle thresholds.
The principal ambiguities are authority resolution, session lifecycle, command failures, flaky-result treatment, redaction exceptions, scale limits, migration, and pass criteria.
